## Diagnosis

### Evidence: bind conflict is silently swallowed

**File: `src/VisualRelay.App/Services/ControlServer.cs`, lines 37–68**

The `Start()` method wraps the entire Kestrel bind+start in a single `try/catch (Exception)` block. When the port is already in use, `app.StartAsync()` throws (the exception type varies by OS — `IOException` on macOS/Linux, `SocketException` on Windows), the catch at line 64 logs to stderr and sets `_app = null`:

```csharp
// Line 64-68
catch (Exception ex)
{
    Console.Error.WriteLine($"vr-control: failed to start ({ex.Message}); control API disabled");
    _app = null;
}
```

`BoundPort` (line 19) defaults to `0` and is only set after `StartAsync()` succeeds (lines 53–58). After a bind failure it stays `0`. The caller in `App.axaml.cs` (line 53: `_controlServer.Start()`) never inspects `BoundPort` or any other success indicator — it unconditionally continues. A caller has **no way to distinguish "not started yet" from "start failed."**

The doc comment on line 14 even codifies the intent: *"A startup failure (e.g. port in use) is caught and logged — it never crashes or blocks app startup."*

### Evidence: zero instance identity in the API surface

**File: `src/VisualRelay.App/Services/ControlServer.Routing.cs`, line 58** — the `/health` endpoint returns a hardcoded anonymous object:
```csharp
await WriteJsonAsync(context, Json.Object(("status", "ok"), ("app", "Visual Relay")));
```
No `instanceId`, `pid`, `nonce`, or any distinguishing field.

**File: `src/VisualRelay.App/Services/ControlApi.State.cs`, lines 16–66** — `BuildStateSnapshot()` returns an anonymous object with `rootPath`, `showArchive`, `isBusy`, `pauseRequested`, `statusText`, `backend`, `setupCheck`, `selectedTask`, `tasks[]`, `stages[]`, `commands`, `obsidianBridge`. No `instanceId` field anywhere.

**File: `src/VisualRelay.App/Services/ControlServerOptions.cs`, line 16** — the record has only three fields:
```csharp
public sealed record ControlServerOptions(bool Enabled, int Port, string? Token)
```
No identity field, no bind-conflict env var.

**File: `src/VisualRelay.App/Services/ControlServer.cs`, line 16** — the class itself has no `InstanceId` property:
```csharp
public sealed partial class ControlServer(ControlApi api, ControlServerOptions options) : IDisposable
```

### Evidence: established patterns to follow

**File: `src/VisualRelay.Core/Execution/ActiveTaskLock.cs`, lines 27–33** — existing codebase pattern for GUID + PID identity:
```csharp
var nonce = Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N");
var info = new { task = taskId, pid = Environment.ProcessId, nonce };
```

**File: `src/VisualRelay.App/Services/ControlServerOptions.cs`, lines 20–40** — `FromEnvironment(IEnvironmentAccessor env)` is the established seam for env-var parsing (already used for `VR_CONTROL_DISABLE`, `VR_CONTROL_PORT`, `VR_CONTROL_TOKEN`).

**File: `tests/VisualRelay.Tests/TestDoubles.cs`, lines 13–24** — `DictionaryEnvironmentAccessor` is the existing test double for env-var injection.

### Evidence: affected test assertions

Every test that reads `/health` asserts the exact current JSON shape, and every `/state` test asserts the presence of fields in `BuildStateSnapshot()`:

| Test file | Line(s) | What it asserts |
|---|---|---|
| `ControlServerTests.cs` | 129–130 | `status == "ok"`, `app == "Visual Relay"` on health |
| `ControlServerKestrelHandlerTests.cs` | 78–80 | Same health assertions |
| `ControlServerKestrelHandlerTests.cs` | 108 | `status == "ok"` on health with token |
| `ControlServerTests.cs` | 172 | `TryGetProperty("commands", out _)` on state |
| `ControlServerKestrelTests.cs` | 101 | `TryGetProperty("commands", out _)` on state |
| `ControlApiTests.cs` | 41–81 | Top-level state fields (`rootPath`, `showArchive`, `isBusy`, etc.) |
| `ControlApiTests.cs` | 102–103 | `pauseRequested` value after toggle |
| `ControlApiTests.cs` | 155 | `rootPath` value after open-folder |
| `ControlRoutes.cs` | 21 | Doc string hardcodes `{"status":"ok","app":"Visual Relay"}` |

All these tests are **additive-safe** — adding new fields (`instanceId`, etc.) won't break existing assertions, but adding a new env var or changing bind behavior will require new tests.

### Reproducer

The silent failure can be reproduced by occupying the control port before app startup:

```bash
# Terminal 1: hold the default port
python3 -c "import socket; s=socket.socket(); s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1); s.bind(('127.0.0.1',8765)); s.listen(1); input('press enter to release')"

# Terminal 2: start the app — the control server fails silently, 
# only a stderr line is emitted, and the app continues as if nothing is wrong.
```

The identity gap can be reproduced by hitting `/health` and `/state` on any running instance — neither endpoint returns a field that distinguishes this process from another instance that might be running concurrently.
